selection_rationale: c1 most directly and feasibly tests the core gap (Q2/G3) — whether canonical verifiers materially reduce undetected operational faults for LLM→config pipelines — with a falsifiable design, manageable compute, and high venue relevance. It balances experimental clarity and impact while remaining implementable within available resources and the CNSM short‑paper scope.
unresolved_uncertainties: Verifier vendor/dialect coverage and resulting systematic false negatives in real vendor configs.
Fidelity gap between emulation (Mininet/containerized routers) and production device behavior.
Adequacy of a 60‑task corpus for external validity (power and task diversity).
Impact of hosted‑model nondeterminism and rate limits on paired comparisons and reproducibility.
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Specify exact verifier(s) and versions (e.g., Batfish vX.Y, NetKAT vX), list supported vendor dialects and how unsupported dialects are handled.
Provide emulation artifact packaging: Docker images, exact container/router images, hashes, and deploy scripts; justify emulator fidelity vs production.
Pre-register exact prompt templates, model identifiers (provider/model name/version), random seeds (where supported), retry policy, and record model-call metadata (timestamps, response IDs).
Perform and document a power analysis to justify the 60‑task sample or adjust task count; stratify tasks by topology complexity and policy type.
Define formal treatment of verifier false positives/negatives, thresholding rules, and pre-specified sensitivity analyses.
Provide detailed logging and archives: raw prompts/responses, verifier traces, emulation logs, and hashes; include replay scripts for full reproducibility.
